buyer.rubric: The positive buyer is the technology leader who owns the budget and authority to bring a contractor onto their own team without routing the decision through a staffing intermediary: CTO, CIO, Head of IT, Head of Technology, IT Director, VP or Head of Engineering, General Manager Technology, Director of Technology, or Chief Customer and Information Officer. Influencers who shape but do not own this decision include engineering managers, delivery or program leads, and enterprise architects who identify the need for a contractor but must get sign-off from the technology leader above them. Hard negatives are senior titles that carry no authority over this specific purchase: HR, talent acquisition, people and culture, procurement and vendor management leaders, and any individual contributor, sales or marketing role, all of whom either sit outside the technology function or manage a different kind of spend. In smaller technology functions within an otherwise large enterprise, a single Head of Technology or IT Director may hold this authority alone, while in the largest ASX-listed groups the decision may sit one level down with a VP or Director of Engineering reporting into the CIO, so both levels should be treated as in-scope.

seller.competitorTest: A competitor in this space sells staffing, labour-hire or contractor-resourcing services to businesses and other agencies that want to outsource the hiring relationship itself, rather than to a client that wants to own and run that hiring relationship in-house.

description: Milestone IT's buyers are large Australian organisations, or the Australian arm of a global group, that run an in-house technology function and hire IT contractors directly into that function rather than outsourcing the hiring process itself; the test for any candidate account is not whether it operates in IT, but whether it owns the end relationship with the technology talent it engages, meaning it holds the budget and authority to bring a contractor onto its own team rather than sourcing that talent through another intermediary. The qualifying shape is 201 or more employees and $100M or more in annual revenue, headquartered or operating a genuine technology team in Australia, with a strong preference for Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane, Perth and Canberra. There is a dead zone below the enterprise tier: mid-market and smaller businesses that lack a standing in-house technology team are treated as cold, because Milestone's model depends on a client with an internal team large enough to absorb contractors directly rather than a business that would need a managed staffing arrangement. Fitting verticals include banking and financial services, fintech, wealth platforms, insurers and superannuation funds, retail, telecommunications, and corporate and enterprise groups in energy, utilities, transport, logistics, healthcare, mining services and ASX-listed groups generally. Excluded are recruitment, staffing and labour-hire firms, IT contractor resellers and RPOs, councils and government bodies locked into supplier panels, and any organisation below the size floor; the category this profile must not chase is any business whose own contractor and staffing needs are met by outsourcing the hiring relationship to a third-party agency rather than running that relationship in-house, since that is a different buyer entirely. Strong signals include a page describing an announced ERP upgrade or core-systems replacement, ideally dated within the last 6 months; a press release or LinkedIn post announcing a new CTO or CIO within the last 12 months; a live job posting for a contract developer, cloud, DevOps, SRE, platform, data or integration engineer, business analyst, tester, project manager, or ERP/Power Platform specialist, current within the last 30 days; an investor or analyst note speaking positively about a bank, fund or insurer's growth plans, dated within the last 3 months; a company announcement of a newly stood-up technology function or digital team, within the last 12 months; a leadership page confirming a Head of IT, Head of Technology, IT Director, VP/Head of Engineering, GM Technology or Director of Technology role exists, checked within the last 6 months; and a careers page or contractor marketplace listing showing the company already engages contract technology staff, current within the last 3 months.

requirements.text: The company has 201 or more employees and at least $100M in annual revenue.
The company is headquartered in Australia or operates a genuine technology team in Australia.
The company runs an in-house technology function that itself holds the budget and authority to engage contractors directly onto its own team.

The company is not a recruitment, staffing, labour-hire, RPO firm, an IT services, consulting or managed-services firm, an IT contractor reseller, or a council/government body locked into supplier panels.
The company is headquartered or based in one of Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane, Perth or Canberra.
The company has a page describing an announced ERP upgrade or core-systems replacement.
The company has a press release or LinkedIn post announcing a new CTO or CIO.
The company has a live job posting for a contract developer, cloud, DevOps, SRE, platform, data, integration engineer, business analyst, tester, project manager, or ERP/Power Platform specialist.
The company is the subject of an investor or analyst note speaking positively about its growth plans.
The company has announced the stand-up of a new technology function or digital team.
The company's leadership page confirms an existing Head of IT, Head of Technology, IT Director, VP/Head of Engineering, GM Technology or Director of Technology role.
The company's careers page or contractor marketplace listing shows it already engages contract technology staff.
